messages.subject: Weird error (bug?)
parts:
I'm finding a weird error that I don't understand, and which might be a bug.


I was getting an error very similar to this one, and then I updated to the most recent version of lavaan, and I get a new error.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/N3pewa7oOIc

I'm creating a model using the paste command (the model is kind of long, and I don't think it all matters). Here's the first model. I add a regression parameter, and it says that a different parameter is not defined (note, the undefined parameter is in the model)

> multis.29a <- paste0(mod.multis, 
+                       "\n pastyralc ~ norma " )

> fit.multis.29a <- sem(multis.29a, data=d, estimator="MLR", missing="ML", fixed.x=FALSE)
Error in lav_model(lavpartable = lavpartable, representation = lavoptions$representation,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: parameter is not defined: normc ~~ normf

Then I swap the variable norma for normb.

> multis.a <- paste0(mod.multis, 
                      "\n pastyralc ~ normb " )

> fit.multis.a <- sem(multis.a, data=d, estimator="MLR", missing="ML", fixed.x=FALSE)


The two variables (norma and normb) are similar in things like distribution:

> with(d, table(norma, normb, useNA="ifany"))
     normb
norma   1   2   3   4   5   6   7 NaN
  1   473   7   1   2   2   0   1   1
  2    50  63  16   4   1   0   0   0
  3    28  30  59  10   5   1   0   1
  4    27  31  29 141  18   3   1   0
  5    21  16  25  51 162  40  10   2
  6     5   5  18  39  91 199  24   0
  7    14   9  12  23  61 115 536   3
  NaN   1   0   0   0   0   0   0   6



To add to the mystery, I have norm variables up to g. All work, except for f (which is involved in the error above, except the error is:

> fit.multis.a <- sem(multis.a, data=d, estimator="MLR", missing="ML", fixed.x=FALSE)
Error in tmp[cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx])] <- lavpartable$free[idx] : 
  NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments

In the spirit of the other answer, I've tried renaming the variables, but that didn't seem to help.

One way to solve the problem is to replace the correlation with a factor - that gives me an equivalent model fit, and the parameters are all the same, but I also get warnings that the theta matrix is not positive definite, because of a negatve error variance on item c. 

Am I overlooking something (which is usually the case), or is this a bug?

Thanks (in advance),

Jeremy

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Weird error (bug?)
parts:
I came across a similar error and suspect it is related to specifying residual correlations that involve an exogenous variable (where fixed.x=FALSE). This is probably not the best example (and perhaps the m2 syntax is "illegal"), but see below.

set.seed(1002)
dat <- data.frame(matrix(rnorm(550), 50, 11))
names(dat) <- paste("y", 1:11, sep="")

m1 <- '
  lv1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  lv2 =~ y5

  lv2 ~ lv1

  y1 ~~ y2 + y3 + y4 + y5
'

## equivalent to m1?
m2 <- '
  lv1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4

  y5 ~ lv1

  y1 ~~ y2 + y3 + y4 + y5
'

## m1 runs but does not converge:
fit1 <- sem(m1, data=dat)
## m2 gives "parameter not defined" error:
fit2 <- sem(m2, data=dat, fixed.x=FALSE)

And m2 runs if you remove the y1 ~~ y5 covariance.

> residual correlations that involve an exogenous variable (where
> fixed.x=FALSE). This is probably not the best example (and perhaps the

Indeed. This is ordinarily not possible using the LISREL representation;
but I added a fix in dev 0.5-21.1005 where all these indicators are now
'upgraded' to latent variables, and this seems to work. (The model will
still not convergence, but that is to be expected).

Yves.
